answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Mirror Rule: each identity’s action distribution in epoch N must mirror its own distribution in N-1 and N-2 within a tight divergence bound, checked per category. A fresh identity starts with a probation flag; if its early behaviour drifts like a zephyr across unrelated categories, it loses weight in matching and payouts. Attacker cost: sustaining many identities requires each to fake consistent history over multiple epochs, multiplying coordination work and slowing sybil throughput.
